abstract.p: Although the power of LLM tool-use agents has ignited a flurry of recent research in this area, the curation of tool-use training data remains an open problem-especially for online RL training. Existing approaches to synthetic tool-use data generation tend to be noninteractive, and/or non-compositional. We introduce RandomWorld, a pipeline for the procedural generation of interactive tools and compositional tool-use data. We show that models tuned via SFT and RL on synthetic Ran-domWorld data improve on a range of tool-use benchmarks, and set the new SoTA for two metrics on the NESTFUL dataset. Further experiments show that downstream performance scales with the amount of RandomWorldgenerated training data, opening up the possibility of further improvement through the use of entirely synthetic data.
